newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen stocks end up on earnings hopes.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen stocks end up on earnings hopes.

text.p: Shenzhen's A and B share indices ended higher in active trading on Wednesday due to buying in shares expected to post solid 1996 earnings, brokers said.
The B share index gained 0.87 points or 0.58 percent to 151.74 on turnover of HK$97 million, up from HK$85 million on Tuesday.
The A share index rose 8.69 points or 2.36 percent to 377.40, with turnover swelling to 7.40 billion yuan from 6.35 billion.

"Prices rose on investors' optimism over China's economy, given Beijing's decision to keep retail price inflation below six percent in 1997," said Song Bin, an analyst with Central-South Securities Co said.
"Investors increased their positions in counters expected to post good 1996 results," he said. "But the market is slightly over-bought, so there is some profit-taking looming."
"The impact of Deng Xiaoping's death on the stock market has faded away with his funeral ceremony on Tuesday," a broker said.
On the B share market, refrigerator maker Hefei Meilin traded most on 3.13 million shares and rose HK$0.22 or 3.62 percent to HK$6.30, making it the strongest performer.
Brokers attributed the rise to expectations of a solid earnings growth for the company in 1996.
Foshan Electrical and Lighting put on HK$0.22 or 3.24 percent to HK$7.01 on the same reason, with 302,450 shares traded.
Chengdu Taikang Chemical Fibre Co debuted on Shenzhen's A share market with a listing of 27.30 million shares, ending the session at 11.08 yuan.

Xiamen Xinda Co Ltd listed 65 million A shares in Shenzhen on Wednesday. The stock closed the session at 11.75 yuan, compared with an offer price of four yuan per share. Volume was the day's heaviest at 39.29 million shares.
